title: Perimenopause 101 — Meera, 44: the cycle log that got her diagnosed
caption:
Perimenopause starts while your periods still come — and it lasts a median 7.4 years (SWAN, JAMA Intern Med 2015).
No blood test diagnoses it — cycle + symptom history does (ACOG).
What changed first?
www.aiforheratx.org

scenes.text: My cycle went *haywire* at 44 — and I was told I'm too young.

scenes.text: After 45, ACOG says the diagnosis comes from your symptoms and cycle history, not a blood test.
phrases: FSH swings day to day, so one "normal" result proves nothing.
After 45, ACOG diagnoses perimenopause from symptoms and cycle history.
Mood dips belong to this transition too — a therapist can help you carry it.
Meera's notebook became the evidence her doctor could finally act on.

scenes.text: Tonight: log cycle day, sleep hours and your top 2 symptoms; tomorrow, walk 30 minutes.
phrases: Tonight, note your cycle day, hours slept, and top 2 symptoms.
Bring two cycles of that log to your clinician — it is the evidence.
Add 150 minutes of moderate movement a week (WHO) for mood, sleep and bones.
